h1:
Hua Hin Beach Clubs
10 Beachfront Spots With Sea Views
intro: Hua Hin and Cha-am are the kind of beach pair where you can sit and catch the sea breeze for hours, from beach clubs with infinity pools to seafood spots with chairs right on the sand. We picked 10 places that are actually open right now, all with seats facing the water and good for a breezy dinner, with notes on the area, rough prices and a few straight-talking tips. One thing to know upfront: Hua Hin's beach faces east, so the sun rises over the sea in the morning. In the evening you get soft golden light and a sky that slowly shifts colour, not the sun dropping straight into the water.

blocks.html: The beachfront scene in Hua Hin splits roughly into two styles. The first is hotel beach clubs with swimming pools, daybeds and cocktail bars, ideal for settling in from afternoon to evening. The other is seafood spots and open-air restaurants that set their tables down close to the sand, leaning on fresh seafood and easier prices. Both work for a breezy dinner; they just differ on budget and vibe.

Most of our picks sit in the Hua Hin–Cha-am stretch, which you can drive in a single line. Some are inside upscale resorts, others are standalone spots along the beach road. We'd suggest checking opening hours and calling ahead to book a seaside table, because the front-row tables fill up fast on weekend evenings.

blocks.text: The beach clubs and beachfront spots we picked

items.name: COAST Beach Club & Bistro (Centara Grand)
items.blurb: A beach club under the Centara Grand on Hua Hin beach, with plenty of open-air seating and clear views out to sea. The menu runs Mediterranean and seafood, wood-fired pizza and grills. Come in the late afternoon for a cocktail in the golden light. It opens in two sittings, lunch and dinner.
items.meta: Hua Hin beach · dinner ~19:00–23:00 · book ahead

items.name: Beach Society (SO Sofitel Hua Hin)
items.blurb: The beachfront spot at SO Sofitel on the Cha-am side, decked out in bold colours in true brand style. Seats sit right on the sand with a wide view of the Gulf of Thailand. The menu leans on well-made food, wine and cocktails. Good for couples or a special meal; the budget runs higher but the setting earns it.
items.meta: Cha-am · inside the resort · good for special meals

items.name: Baba Beach Club Hua Hin (by Sri panwa)
items.blurb: A music-leaning beach club on the Cha-am side, with a big footprint, clean sand and a long pool looking out to sea. The draw is the sound system and DJs. The bar and restaurant run all day serving Asian and international dishes, plus grills from the Josper. Good for party people who want to stay put well into the evening.
items.meta: Cha-am · open all day · music/party crowd

items.name: Sundance Dayclub Hua Hin
items.blurb: A newer dayclub in the Hua Hin–Cha-am zone. The selling point is an infinity pool around 40 metres long that seems to run straight into the horizon, plus cabanas, a swim-up bar and European fusion food. You enter on a day pass, so it works for an afternoon that rolls into dinner.
items.meta: Hua Hin–Cha-am · day pass · infinity pool
items.price: day pass / minimum spend, check the booking page

items.name: Oceanside Beach Club & Restaurant
items.blurb: An easygoing beachfront spot with seats on the sand and events that come and go, like barbecue brunches, tapas nights or themed beach parties. The food and drinks cover plenty of ground, so it suits groups of friends who want both the food and the atmosphere.

items.name: Let's Sea Hua Hin
items.blurb: The beachfront restaurant at Let's Sea resort, relaxed in feel with seats right by the water. The food mixes Thai and international, with sea bass dishes and signature cocktails standing out. Good for a quiet dinner without the noise.
items.meta: Hua Hin beach · inside the resort · quiet vibe

items.name: Baan Dum Oceanfront Seafood
items.blurb: A seafood spot in an old Thai-style house on the Hua Hin shore, where nearly every table has a wide view of the Gulf. It leans on proper Thai-style seafood, fresh from the sea, with friendly service. Good for anyone who wants both the view and serious Thai flavours.
items.meta: Hua Hin beach · Thai seafood · sea view from most tables

items.name: Chay Had Beach Front Restaurant
items.blurb: A beachfront spot in a good location, with open-air seating close to the water. It serves local Thai food, both seafood and dishes from the land, in a homey, laid-back setting at prices easier than the hotel side.
items.meta: Hua Hin beach · local Thai food · easy budget

items.name: Azure (InterContinental Hua Hin)
items.blurb: The seafood restaurant at the InterContinental, built around local ingredients, with seafood from the fishing villages nearby and produce and meat from farms close by. The seaside setting is polished, so it suits a finer dinner.
items.meta: Hua Hin beach · inside the resort · local-sourced seafood

items.name: Ton Seafood Restaurant
items.blurb: A beachfront seafood spot near the pier with a relaxed, local feel. The seafood is fresh and well seasoned, and reviews point to good service and fair prices. Good for a simple dinner with a sea view.
items.meta: Hua Hin beach · near the pier · local spot

blocks.title: Tips for booking a seaside table
blocks.html: The front-row tables with a full sea view are usually limited, so if you want one, call ahead and say you'd like a table by the water, especially on Friday-to-Sunday evenings and long weekends. For beach clubs with a day pass, check the minimum-spend terms before you go.

blocks.text: What the evening light is like in Hua Hin

blocks.html: Because Hua Hin's beach faces east, the sun rises over the sea in the morning, so anyone who wants to see it come up straight out of the water has to be up early. In the evening, what you get is soft golden light with the sky slowly turning orange and pink behind the restaurants, which is lovely and photographs well, but it isn't the sun sinking into the sea like on the Andaman side. We say this plainly so you set your expectations right.

items: Want the sunrise over the sea — come early, about 20–30 minutes before first light. Hua Hin beach is great for this.
Want the golden evening light — sit down for dinner around 17:30–18:30 for the soft light and the colour-changing sky.
Want to keep the party going — pick a music-leaning beach club that stays open late, so you get both dinner and the night-time atmosphere.

blocks.text: How to pick the right one for your trip

items.name: Couples / special meals
items.blurb: Go for a resort restaurant like Beach Society, Let's Sea or Azure. Quiet setting, careful service, a higher budget but worth the feel.

items.name: Groups of friends / chilling
items.blurb: COAST, Sundance or Oceanside give you a pool, a bar and plenty of seating, so you can settle in from afternoon to evening.

items.name: Seafood on an easy budget
items.blurb: Baan Dum, Chay Had or Ton Seafood for fresh seafood and a sea view at prices easier than the hotel side.

faq.q: Which Hua Hin beach clubs actually have tables right by the sea?
faq.a: For seats with a full sea view, try COAST Beach Club at the Centara Grand, Beach Society at SO Sofitel on the Cha-am side, and Baba Beach Club with its wide private beach. For more budget-friendly seafood, Baan Dum and Chay Had also set their tables close to the sand. We'd suggest calling ahead to book a seaside table.

faq.q: Can you watch the sunset at Hua Hin beach?
faq.a: Hua Hin's beach faces east, so you see the sun rise over the sea in the morning. In the evening you get soft golden light and a colour-changing sky behind the restaurants, not the sun sinking straight into the water. If you want the sea in the morning, come before first light.

faq.q: What's the budget for a beachfront dinner in Hua Hin?
faq.a: Local beachfront seafood spots start around THB 300–700 per person, while beach clubs and resort restaurants tend to run from about THB 900–2,000 per person, depending on the drinks and dishes you order. Prices are rough estimates, so check the current menu at the venue.

faq.q: Do Hua Hin beach clubs charge an entry fee or a minimum spend?
faq.a: Beach clubs with pools and daybeds, like some dayclubs, often have a day-pass fee or a per-head minimum spend, while regular beachfront restaurants just charge for what you order. We'd suggest checking the terms on the booking page or calling to ask before you go.

faq.q: Are the beach clubs different in Hua Hin versus Cha-am?
faq.a: They sit on the same stretch and you can drive between them. The Cha-am side tends to have big resorts with wide beaches like SO Sofitel and Baba Beach Club, while the Hua Hin side mixes hotel beach clubs with local seafood spots. Choose by budget and the style you're after.
